tweet.text:
Vals AI tested whether a team of AI coding agents beats one agent, and mostly it did not.

Vals gave GPT 6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 the same 50 web app builds from its Vibe Code Bench. Each model ran alone and as a team, where a lead agent hands work to up to five subagents. Both ran at medium and max reasoning effort.

Teams cost 1.8 to 5.1 times as much as a single agent. Only one of the four score changes was statistically significant: Sol at medium effort, up 7.3 points to 84.9 percent. The other three changes ran from minus 0.3 to plus 3.4 points.

For Sol, max effort on a single agent added 11.4 points, more than the 7.3 a team added at medium. Opus scored 91.5 percent as a single agent at medium effort for 4.08 dollars an app. Its max effort team scored 93.2 percent, the highest in the study, at 122 dollars an app.

My read: the team trick is cheap for one model and costly for the other. Sol's medium team paid 1.85 dollars more (3.07 minus 1.22) for 7.3 points, about 25 cents a point. Opus's max effort team paid 98.23 dollars more (122 minus 23.77) than its max effort single agent. That bought 3.4 points, about 29 dollars a point, and Vals says the gain was not significant.

https://www.vals.ai/blogs/multi-agent-vibe-code-bench
